newsitem.title: CHINA: China capital boosts control of films and tapes.
newsitem.headline: China capital boosts control of films and tapes.

text.p: China's capital Beijing has passed new rules aimed at clamping down on the copyright theft of audio-visual products and at curbing violent, pornographic or subversive content, the Xinhua news agency said.
The Beijing municipal legislature on Friday approved the regulations, which would go into force in January, 1998, the agency said in an overnight report.
Under the rules, dealers in audio-visual products would be required to obtain a special certificate, which would be revoked if they acted improperly, it said.
The regulations also banned the public showing of video tapes intended for individuals, in order to protect their copyright, it said.
Video and audio products that disrupted national unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity, leaked state secrets, or were violent, superstitious or pornographic, were also banned, it said.
Beijing currently has more than 2,000 shops selling audio-visual products and some 1.7 million illegal compact discs, video tapes, and cassettes had been confiscated in the city since 1994, it said.
